title: Garden and Sigil
premise: Bram Nakamura has survived the Vellum Guild's cutthroat world by mapping realms no one else can reach and keeping his name off every ledger. When a dying courier forces a blood-inked map into his hands—a map of the Hollow King's own mind—Bram becomes the only living person who can see the parasite wearing the king's crown. Hunted by the Guild's enforcers and the thing on the throne alike, Bram must ally with the stranger's sister, a disgraced sigil-witch, and descend into the unmapped country inside the king's head. In the end Bram unbinds the king at the cost of his own invisibility, choosing to be known, named, and hunted—because a life unlived in hiding was never really survival.
about_author: August Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing impossible maps in university special collections before turning to fiction. Hartwell writes fantasy obsessed with paper, memory, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Bram Nakamura, POV. In the Vellum Guild's fog-bound countinghouse, Bram maps a realm that exists only on Tuesdays while concealing his own name from the ledgers. He prides himself on being untraceable. Emotional beat: the smug comfort of a man who believes invisibility is safety—right before it fails.

chapters.title: Blood in the Inkwell
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. A courier collapses at Bram's door, bleeding black ink, and presses a folded map into his hands with a warning: the king is not the king. The map is drawn in living blood and shows not geography but the interior of a mind. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility as the courier dies naming Bram.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Studying the blood-map, Bram recognizes cartographic techniques only he uses—someone taught the dying courier his own secret methods. The map's margins contain a sigil that moves when unobserved. Emotional beat: vertigo as Bram realizes his hidden craft has been stolen and weaponized.

chapters.title: The Guild Sends Regards
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Guild enforcers arrive asking after a stolen ledger; Bram lies badly and burns his own safehouse ledgers to hide the blood-map. His carefully constructed anonymity begins collapsing. Emotional beat: panic, the first crack in his belief that hiding equals surviving.

chapters.title: A Witch Named Sorrel
chapters.summary: Sorrel Vance, POV. The courier's sister, a sigil-witch expelled from her order, ambushes Bram demanding the map. She reveals her brother stole it from the royal archive to save the king. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into fury, and grudging recognition between two people who both live in disguise.

chapters.title: Terms of an Uneasy Pact
chapters.summary: Bram and Sorrel, alternating. They strike a bargain: Bram reads the map, Sorrel supplies the sigil-lore to act on it. She warns that blood-maps bind the reader—already Bram dreams in the map's geography. Emotional beat: wary alliance, the first warmth Bram has allowed himself in years.

chapters.title: The City That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sorrel, POV. Fleeing Guild enforcers through the capital, Sorrel uses forbidden sigils to hide them, and the city's old stones whisper the true history of the Hollow King's coronation. Emotional beat: Sorrel's guilt over her brother's death hardening into resolve to finish what he started.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. At a royal procession, Bram sees through the blood-map's lens: the king's body moves, but something vast and patient looks out of his eyes. It notices Bram noticing. Emotional beat: cold terror—the parasite has seen him, and invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Summoned to court under pretense of commissioning a map, Bram walks the palace where the walls are subtly wrong, mapped by something that eats boundaries. He meets the king, who slips him a whispered plea for help. Emotional beat: pity and horror entwined—the king is a prisoner in his own skull.

chapters.title: The Price of the First Door
chapters.summary: Sorrel, POV. To open a passage into the king's mind, Sorrel must carve a sigil into living skin—hers—and pay a memory as toll. She loses her memory of her brother's face. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; survival and rescue both cost pieces of the self.

chapters.title: Into the Mapped Mind
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram enters the king's mindscape using the blood-map as a guide: a country of drowned archives and roads that remember being walked. He finds the king's true self, small and buried. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into urgency—the mindscape is being eaten from the edges.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Original Sin
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. In the mindscape's archive, Bram discovers his old master drew the first blood-map—and taught the parasite how to wear a king. His inheritance of craft is also inheritance of guilt. Emotional beat: devastating recognition that his lineage built the cage he now must break.

chapters.title: What Sorrel Gave Up
chapters.summary: Sorrel, POV. Outside, Sorrel holds the sigil-door open while enforcers close in, losing more memories with each hour. She fights beside an old order rival who offers restoration of her memories if she abandons Bram. Emotional beat: temptation of self-preservation versus loyalty—she refuses.

chapters.title: The King Who Was Left
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram speaks with the buried true king, who confesses he invited the parasite in to survive a coup, trading his self for his body's survival. Emotional beat: bitter empathy—Bram sees his own philosophy of hiding taken to its logical, monstrous end.

chapters.title: The Guild's True Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Escaping the mindscape, Bram learns the Vellum Guild has brokered the possession for centuries, trading stability for sovereignty. His name has been in their ledgers since birth—he was never invisible, only unread. Emotional beat: fury and liberation; the myth of his own safety dies.

chapters.title: Sigil and Counter-Sigil
chapters.summary: Sorrel, POV. Sorrel and Bram design the unbinding rite: it requires the parasite's true name, which exists only in the burned original ledger. They plan a heist of the Guild's deepest vault. Emotional beat: hope with teeth—two liars and thieves preparing their most honest work.

chapters.title: The Vault of Names
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. The vault heist: Bram maps the unmappable vault by feel while Sorrel holds off enforcers with sigils that cost her her past. They retrieve the ledger and learn the parasite's name—and that it can only be unbound from inside the king. Emotional beat: breathless triumph shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Crown's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Bram and Sorrel, alternating. The parasite strikes back, seizing Sorrel through her carved sigil and using her voice to lure Bram into a trap. Bram must cut her free, wounding the door sigil and closing their way in. Emotional beat: despair—the plan broken, the cost already unbearable.

chapters.title: The Last Map
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. With no way in but himself, Bram draws a new blood-map in his own blood, making his mind the door. Sorrel protests; he argues this is the first thing he has ever chosen to be seen doing. Emotional beat: quiet resolve—identity embraced as the price of the attempt.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, inside the king. Bram confronts the parasite in the drowned archive of the king's mind, speaking its true name and offering it a trade: a mapped realm of its own, honestly bounded, instead of a stolen life. The king's self reasserts. Emotional beat: the climax—cunning and compassion defeating possession.

chapters.title: The King in His Garden
chapters.summary: Sorrel, POV. The restored king, remembering everything, dismantles the Guild's charter and offers Bram protection Bram doesn't want. Sorrel's memories return in fragments, imperfect but hers. Emotional beat: bittersweet aftermath; rescue succeeded, but nothing returns unmarked.

chapters.title: Garden and Sigil
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram declines a court title and instead opens a small school of cartography under his own name, teaching openly what he once hid. Sorrel plants a garden over the site of the old vault. Emotional beat: resolution—Bram learns that being known is not the same as being owned, and inheritance can be remade.
